impact: Trigger: a transient build failure (disk full, git lock, network share), the operator fixes the cause and presses refresh in the TUI or runs layers block. Outcome: for up to five minutes the old error comes back with no retry and no hint why; only the CLI help documents the window, and only the CLI refresh can pass --force.
suggested_fix: Pass force: true from the TUI refresh argv; add the window and --force to the PackageGraphError message and to the graph: line of the detail view (failed at <time>, retried automatically after 5 minutes, or run refresh --force); let ensurePackageLayers take a force option for callers that mean it.

problem: The per-page guard in wikiFor that records an unreadable wiki page is not pinned: deleting it leaves the focused suite green. The guard is real (collectPages already read every page, so only a page removed or chmod-ed between the two reads reaches it) but no test can reach that state without a reader seam.
impact: Trigger: a page disappears or loses its mode between collectPages and the second readFile. Outcome: with the guard gone the page is dropped without a word and the section is reported as read with fewer items, the exact silent-empty case AC2 exists to prevent, and no test would notice a regression.
suggested_fix: Give wikiFor a readPage seam defaulting to readFile and pin the message 'N of M wiki page(s) could not be read', or have collectPages return the content it read so the second read and the guard disappear together.

problem: withDetachedWorktree unregisters its cleanup before awaiting it. A signal that arrives while the awaited git worktree remove runs finds no registered cleanup, so the handler removes the lock and re-raises while the removal is cut off.
impact: Trigger: SIGTERM or SIGINT during the post-build worktree removal. Outcome: the worktree registration and the keryx-layers temp directory are left behind until the next refresh sweeps them after the sweep age.
suggested_fix: Await cleanup() first and unregister in a nested finally, so the registered cleanup stays visible to the handler for as long as it runs; the cleanup is idempotent.
evidence: Executed probe (order-probe.test.ts): git remove held for 400 ms, SIGTERM sent while it ran; afterwards 2 registered worktrees and a leftover keryx-layers-* directory. layers.ts:409-410.

problem: The signal handler awaits every registered cleanup with no bound, so a hung git worktree remove keeps the process alive after SIGTERM.
impact: Trigger: SIGTERM while git blocks. Outcome: the process does not die by the signal until git returns; a second signal or SIGKILL still ends it, so nothing leaks.
suggested_fix: Race the cleanups against a short timer (a few seconds) before the lock removal and the re-raise.
